short: Four assaults over four months to break the German line south of Rome.
full:
The Gustav Line ran across Italy at its narrowest point, hinged on the Rapido valley and on the mountain crowned by the sixth-century abbey of Monte Cassino. Allied attacks began on 17 January 1944, and the Anzio landing eight days later, meant to unhinge the position from behind, produced a second besieged beachhead instead. On 15 February the abbey was destroyed by 1,400 tons of bombs on the assumption that it was occupied; the Germans had stayed out of it, and paratroopers then fortified the ruins.

American, British, Indian, New Zealand, French colonial and Polish formations attacked in turn across ground overlooked from above. The final assault opened on 11 May, with French Moroccan troops turning the line through the Aurunci mountains, and Polish II Corps took the ruined abbey on 18 May. Casualties came to around 55,000 Allied and 20,000 German. Rome fell on 4 June, two days before the Normandy landings pushed the Italian campaign out of the headlines for good.
